gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Round bowls drawn like bent tubing give Azonix a wide, commanding stance, though its words take a moment to knit back together. Noto Sans Nabataean, a plain sans with lowercase nearly cap-tall, reads smoothly after it.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-nag-munda: Noto Sans Nag Mundari looks half unwrapped in its curves. Azonix is the one built to command attention with its uniform, wide-mouthed capitals, while the body font earns its keep with lowercase that rivals the capitals.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-nandinaga: Azonix draws each stroke as stout as a pipe cleaner, giving its capitals a commanding, almost mechanical presence. And Noto Sans Nandinagari, with short ascenders and generous openings, softens the page into something approachable.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-newa: Noto Sans Newa has a clearly open mouth on its lowercase e. Over a full page its tall bowls and counters read smoothly, a modern texture that never fights the single-tip simplicity of Azonix above.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Contemporary and tall, the body sets the tone. Azonix commands the top with lines like bent rope, while Noto Sans Nushu holds its terminals far from the stroke and towers with an enormous x-height beneath.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Azonix draws every letter with a tube-like, constant-width stroke, wide and authoritative with capitals barely above the lowercase. Noto Sans Ogham follows, its tall bodies looking bold and its e wide open, a plain sans counterweight.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Rounded wire, wide and bold. Azonix stands up top with a commanding edge, and Noto Sans Ol Chiki settles under it with curve tails held well back, so words read as solid blocks.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-old-hunga: Azonix has a thin-free, swell-free stroke, a commanding display look that is crisp even when shrunk. Noto Sans Old Hungarian is the one for sustained reading, with large open counters in its tall a, e and s.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-old-itali: Azonix has no swelling in its bowls, which gives its wide, commanding letters a rigid, authoritative stance. Noto Sans Old Italic does the quieter work, with curve endings kept well apart.
gen-dafont-azonix-gf-noto-sans-old-north: Azonix has a compass-pencil consistency, with round, uniform strokes and capitals barely above its lowercase. And Noto Sans Old North Arabian packs a dense, tall lowercase band whose outward-pointing terminals keep long stretches of text approachable.
